answer: Each voting key must bind to one exclusive silicon PUF and lock a slashable bond. Enrollment goes on a public raven log, so a cloned or recast chip is obvious. At unscheduled times the protocol issues a short whisper nonce; only that live PUF may answer, and the raw response must land before the window closes. If two keys share a device, a reply is late, or both collapse into the same karst of colliding response maps, every linked deposit is slashed. Fielding N identities requires N distinct chips and N bonds, so silicon and capital scale with farm size.
